decisions.executionNote: Approach the red mouse with the right arm, rising and gradually pitching the open gripper downward; preserve elbow-up continuity.
Align the right gripper vertically over the mouse and approach slowly, leaving clearance for visual refinement.
Lower around the mouse, close fully, and begin a small test lift; grasp retention will be checked visually.
Lift the closed right gripper and transport the mouse toward the pad, checking that it follows rather than sliding.
Mouse remained on the table; reopen and realign over its shifted center before a deeper, centered grasp.
Descend with open jaws around the mouse, close fully at tabletop grasp height, and test retention with a short lift.
Lift the mouse with the right gripper fully closed, then begin translating toward the mouse pad; verify retention from the next views.
The mouse did not remain held. Reopen and approach its new position with a lower, more centered grasp rather than assuming retention.
Use the wrist view to center the mouse between the jaws before closing, then perform a small vertical lift only.
Keep the mouse gripper closed and lift clear, then carry toward the pad while checking the mouse remains between the jaws.
The mouse is still on the table. Return open jaws to its center and lower the grasp to engage beneath the curved upper shell.
Refine lateral centering and engage the lower mouse sides, close fully, then lift vertically to verify an actual grasp.
Mouse now appears seated between the jaws. Keep closed, lift clear, and translate toward the pad without changing grasp orientation.
Carry the retained mouse to the pad center, lower it onto the surface, then release with the gripper open.
Replan after the continuity stop: the mouse is already over the pad, so lower vertically, release, and lift away without further extension.
Leave the released mouse on the pad and retract the right arm; bring both arms toward positions behind the keyboard for a controlled two-sided push.
Position closed grippers low behind the two keyboard corners, keeping each arm in its own workspace and avoiding contact until aligned.
The clock obstructs the keyboard's path. Lift clear and approach the clock with the left arm first; park the right arm safely behind the keyboard.
Move the open left gripper above the clock, finishing a vertical grasp orientation while staying clear of the keyboard.
The wrist view places the clock ahead of the jaws; advance into its center, lower slightly, close fully, and test-lift.
Lift the retained clock clear and carry left toward the drawer, gently relaxing wrist pitch while maintaining the closed grasp and elbow-up configuration.
Carry the clock higher and leftward toward the drawer top, keeping the grasp fixed and leaving clearance above its rim.
After the IK stop, use smaller forward-left increments and relax pitch slightly rather than raising into the tightly folded configuration.
Back away slightly from the constrained high-forward pose while shifting left; keep the clock held and preserve the elbow-up branch before trying the drawer approach again.
Raise the held clock near the drawer front with small increments and a more vertical wrist, retaining clearance and monitoring the tightly bent elbow.
Replan after the continuity guard: relax the downward wrist pitch while advancing only slightly, bringing the held clock above the drawer without a large elbow change.
Avoid the rejected high pose: lower the wrist slightly while rotating the held clock forward, creating elbow margin and raising its lower edge toward the drawer rim.
The last command executed nothing. First lower straight down to regain joint margin, then test a small forward approach while keeping the clock grasp fixed.
Use submillimeter downward increments to leave the near-singular pose after two zero-execution rejections; keep the held clock closed.
Reverse the recent coupled pitch-and-forward motion in small steps to recover the prior continuous elbow-up configuration, keeping the clock securely held.
Use a lower forward approach while gradually changing wrist orientation, avoiding another high-pose singularity before lifting the clock onto the drawer.
With a less constrained wrist orientation, lift the clock vertically above the drawer's front rim while keeping the grasp closed.
The clock clears the front edge. Advance cautiously over the drawer with a slight descent instead of raising farther into the IK limit.
Lower the wrist while rotating the held clock forward onto the drawer, avoiding further high forward extension after the guard stop.
The previous command executed nothing. Retry the lowering-and-pitch adjustment at one-quarter scale to keep joint changes continuous.
The elbow has moved away from its limit. Advance the held clock onto the drawer top with a small descent, keeping the grasp closed until supported.
The clock is over the drawer top. Lower slightly, open the gripper to let it settle, then withdraw backward away from the joint limit.
Withdraw the open left gripper to check whether the clock remains supported, and lower the closed right gripper behind the keyboard for its next push.
Clock remains on the drawer and mouse on the pad. Align both closed grippers just behind the keyboard at a low pushing height.
Push the keyboard gently forward and right with both closed grippers, maintaining level contact and checking translation toward the outline.
Continue the balanced diagonal push toward the keyboard outline, keeping both contacts low and each arm on its own side.
Make a final small forward-right keyboard adjustment, then open and withdraw both grippers to assess its placement without continued contact.
Keyboard is aligned near its frame. Withdraw both arms, return the right toward home, and bring the open left gripper to a clear approach in front of the figurine.
Replan from the interrupted pose with slower right-arm homing increments; align the open left gripper in front of the figurine's torso.
Center the left jaws around the figurine's torso, close fully and test-lift; complete the right arm's gentle return to its starting pose.
The figurine did not lift. Reopen and advance along the gripper approach direction to surround its torso rather than closing in front of it, then test again.
Lift the closed left gripper to verify the figurine is retained, then begin carrying toward its stand while leaving the right arm at home.
The figurine stayed on the table. Reopen and return for a lower torso grasp rather than lifting from its sloping shoulders.
Advance the open jaws around the figurine's narrow waist, close fully, and lift slightly to check retention before carrying.
The closed fingertips were still in front of the torso. Reopen and advance farther along the approach axis to surround the waist before closing again.
The figurine appears enclosed now. Keep the left gripper closed, lift clear, then begin moving toward the small stand while checking retention.
The figurine has lifted from the table. Carry it toward the stand with the grasp closed and a fixed wrist orientation, staying entirely in the left workspace.
The figurine slipped and is lying down. Reopen and switch to an overhead torso grasp, approaching slowly without disturbing the organized keyboard or clock.
Back away from possible drawer contact and rotate the open jaws across the lying figurine's torso before another descent.
Use the wrist view to align the overhead jaws across the figurine's torso, advancing left and forward with a shallow descent.
Tracking suggests contact near the drawer. Back the wrist away and tilt the open gripper toward the lying figurine to reach its torso without pressing the arm into the drawer.
The lying figurine is centered between the jaws. Lower around its torso, close fully, and make a short vertical retention test.
The jaws closed above the lying torso. Reopen and lower substantially to surround its sides, then close and test with a short lift.
Advance the open jaws along their tilted approach axis to engage the lying torso more deeply, then close and test a small vertical lift.
The torso now appears enclosed by the jaws. Keep fully closed and lift vertically clear of the table before attempting to upright the figurine.
The figurine is retained off the table. Begin rotating it upright about the world Y axis while adding clearance beneath its base; maintain the closed grasp.
Continue uprighting the retained figurine and shift slightly toward its stand; keep the base clear and the grasp closed.
The figurine appears to have slipped while uprighting. Withdraw and orient the open left gripper for a low approach in front of it, allowing it to settle before refinement.
The figurine has fallen across the keyboard. Approach its exposed base from the left workspace and try a base grip, avoiding the torso over the keyboard.
Test the base grip by lifting and moving left away from the keyboard, keeping the gripper closed and its orientation fixed.
The base was not retained. Reopen and advance farther to surround its exposed rim before closing, while keeping the left arm clear of the keyboard.
The wrist view shows the rim behind the pinch point. Reopen, back up slightly and lower around the rim before closing again.
Shift the open jaws left to center on the exposed base rather than the legs, close fully, and make a short retention lift.
Keep the gripper closed and lift clear of the keyboard to check whether the base-side grasp retains the figurine before rotating it.
The rim grip did not hold. Approach the exposed torso from above, rotating the open jaws across the body while maintaining clearance and staying left of center.
Finish aligning the open jaws across the lying figurine's waist and approach from above, leaving clearance for a final depth adjustment.
Replan after the continuity guard with smaller translations and fixed orientation; lower the open jaws toward the figurine's waist while moving away from the high-pose limit.
Center the open jaws across the waist, close fully, then lift slightly back and left to test retention without rotating the figurine.
Do not advance farther into the reach limit. Close at the current waist alignment, then move back-left with a small lift to recover margin and check retention.
Replan the rejected retreat at much smaller increments, preserving the closed waist grasp while moving back-left away from the reach limit.
The waist remains between the jaws. Lift clear while retracting left and back to recover elbow margin before any uprighting motion.
Upright the retained figurine gradually while translating the wrist around the waist contact, reducing swinging and keeping the base above the table.
